What does it mean to vectorize?

A PNG or JPG is a raster image: a grid of pixels with a fixed size. An SVG is a vector image: a set of shapes and paths that can be resized while staying crisp.

Vectorization traces the colors and edges in a raster image and redraws them as vector shapes. Flat-color logos and illustrations usually make the cleanest starting point. Photos can become stylized artwork, though a trace is an interpretation rather than a perfect photo copy.

GOOD QUESTIONS

Curious? Let’s clear that up.

Everything you need to know before you make your first vector.

Ready to try it? ↗
How do I convert an image to SVG? +

Choose a PNG, JPG, WebP, or GIF from your device, then select a color count and detail level. Choose “Make my vector” to create a downloadable SVG file.

Can I convert a PNG logo to SVG? +

Yes. Flat-color PNG logos are a good fit for vector tracing. Upload the image, use a smaller color palette for a simpler result, then inspect the SVG before using it in a brand or production workflow.

Will a photo become an exact vector copy? +

Not exactly. A photo contains continuous tones and texture, while an SVG uses shapes. Vectorizing a photo creates an artistic, color-reduced interpretation. The detail and palette controls change the look.

Is my image uploaded or stored? +

The selected image is sent securely to Vectorizer.AI in test mode. This integration requests no retention, and test results are watermarked.

Can I use the SVG for printing or cutting? +

You can download and try the SVG in your design workflow. Compatibility and cleanup needs depend on the software, image, and production method. Review the file in your target app before a print or cutting job.
